title: Remediation lanes and priority scorecard for private network exemptions
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: This ticket defines a structured 'remediation lanes' framework and an accompanying priority scorecard for handling customer requests to deploy Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem / air-gapped) in environments that require network exemptions, staged upgrades, or custom patching windows. The goal is to reduce back-and-forth intake time, standardize technical gates, and give sales/CS clear SLAs for timelines and expected effort.

Scope: 1) Define 3 remediation lanes (Self-Serve, Assisted Remediation, Engineering-Run) with acceptance criteria for each lane. 2) Build a numeric scorecard (0-100) used by intake to prioritize requests along these dimensions: network complexity, security constraints, upgrade delta, business criticality, compliance sensitivity, and available customer resources. 3) Create intake checklist and templated comms for customers and internal stakeholders. 4) Document decision thresholds that map score ranges to remediation lanes and expected SLA windows.

Out of scope: full automation of remediation steps (separate engineering initiatives), pricing changes, and deep-dive network engineering runbooks.

Success metrics: - Median time-to-plan (first actionable plan communicated to customer) reduced from ~10 business days to <= 3 business days for lane-decided requests. - Reduction in ambiguous intake outcomes (fewer than 10% marked 'need more info' after first triage). - Baseline prioritization accuracy: 80% of high-score requests routed to Engineering-Run with correct resourcing estimates vs historical ops decisions.

Acceptance criteria: - Scorecard fields defined and documented. - Example intake completed for 3 recent customer requests (contrasting lanes). - Internal triage runbook and communication templates added to Confluence. - Hand-off checklist for ENG/OPS with estimated hours for each lane.

Proposed remediation lanes (draft):
- Self-Serve (score <= 30): Customer can follow documented steps, standard networking config, supported OS/container images, and routine upgrades. Target SLA: plan within 72 hours; execution by customer with Redwood guidance.
- Assisted Remediation (score 31-65): Requires Redwood Solutions or CS time for network probes, minor config changes, or limited patching coordination. Target SLA: plan within 3 business days; Redwood provides a remediation engineer window within 10 business days.
- Engineering-Run (score > 65): Complex firewalls, strict air-gap constraints, or major upgrades requiring eng resources. Target SLA: plan within 5 business days; resource allocation, cost estimate, and timeline provided within 10 business days.

Scorecard fields (draft):
- Network topology complexity (0-20)
- Firewall and outbound dependency count (0-15)
- Required OS/PKG patching delta (0-10)
- Air-gap / data egress constraints (0-20)
- Compliance/regulatory sensitivity (0-10)
- Customer engineering bandwidth (inverse, 0-15)
- Business criticality / ARR impact (0-10)

Ops notes: weightings are adjustable after 6 weeks of trial. Establish an internal review cadence (bi-weekly) to calibrate thresholds and false positives.

Stakeholders: PM (Asha Patel), Solutions/CS lead (Jordan Reyes), Lead SRE (Priya Nair), Security reviewer (Evan Kline), Design for comms (Rae Kim), Eng owner for automation follow-on (Diego Morales).

Artifacts and links: - Draft Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PD/pages/654321012/Remediation+Lanes+and+Scorecard - Intake template (Google Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cRemediationTemplates - Example intake PRDs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-onboarding/blob/main/docs/intake-examples.md - Customer cases used for examples: PM-24680, PM-35977, PM-32345.
